module: Shared kit for painting groundmodels (physics) on mesh roads (groundmodel mode of the Hero Road Editor). The groundmodel is inferred from the name of a triangle's material: grip variants look the same as the base and differ only by groundType. The variants are the road's pavement material plus a suffix (_wet, _snow or _snowy, _ice); Dry is the base material and serves as an eraser. A state can only be painted if its material exists in the level. The paint is stored in world stamps { x, y, r, m } (m = palette index starting at 1).
notes: Palette: 1 Dry (ASPHALT1), 2 Wet (ASPHALT_WET), 3 Snow (SNOW), 4 Ice (ICE). The colors are only used for the editor overlay.
In materialAt, the stamp with the highest index (painted last) wins, including a Dry eraser stamp.
The spatial grid has a cell equal to the largest brush radius (at least 0.5) and a 3x3 neighborhood search.
materialOf falls back to the base material if the variant does not exist; without baseMat, returns 'dry' (palette id).

get.desc: Palette entry (id, label, groundmodel, col, suffixes).

isBase.desc: True if the index is that of the base surface (Dry); nil is treated as the base.

labelOf.desc: Label of the entry, '?' if unknown.

colOf.desc: Overlay color { r, g, b } (0-255); that of Dry if the index is unknown.

materialExists.desc: True if a material of this name is present in the level (scenetree.findObject).

variantMaterial.desc: Name of the variant material of surface `i` for the pavement `baseMat`, or nil if no variant exists (not paintable). Dry returns the base material.

isAvailable.desc: True if surface `i` is paintable: Dry always, the others only if a variant exists.

materialOf.desc: Material actually applied to a painted quad of surface `i`: the variant if it exists, otherwise the base.

resolveMaterials.desc: Resolves the material of each surface for a given base, in one pass (called once per mesh build).

buildGrid.desc: Builds a uniform spatial hash over the stamps so the per-quad lookup is roughly O(1). Returns nil if nothing is painted.

stamps.desc: List of stamps { x, y, r, m }.

materialAt.desc: Palette index of the painted surface at world point (px, py): the highest-index stamp covering the point wins. Returns the base index if nothing covers it.
